entries.tactical_failure_mode_quoted: The dominant failure is substituting one selection rule for another that performs better empirically while omitting the theorem that explains when and why it wins — reviewers read this as a straightforward engineering combination without structural insight, even when the empirical gains are real. A second shape is pivoting an assumption the community regards as a reasonable modeling choice rather than a genuine restriction (removing an anchor or a repeated-query requirement that practitioners consider natural, or predicting an unmotivated quantity), which leaves both motivation and novelty in doubt.

entries.tactical_pattern_quoted: Every paper here centers on a selection / acquisition / query rule — which instance to keep, which candidate to query, which subset to retain, which component to route to, or when to stop buying information — and pivots the single assumption baked into that rule's criterion or its required structure. The pivot takes one of two concrete forms: relax the structural crutch to a weaker condition and re-prove the guarantee, or reframe the selection task as a different and more tractable problem class and import that class's machinery.

paper_pointed_threat.subsumption_argument: The Gate, Not the Cache reports that at skip ratio 0.9 on LIBERO-Object, reuse and deletion fall to 0.68 and 0.31 respectively versus dense 1.00 when the next gate is harvested from the model's own accelerated forward; the collapse is invisible to the evaluated action-level detectors. This threatens any cache whose validity signal is self-contaminated across control steps. RankSafe instead computes a full candidate canary under the deterministic contract, falls back on mismatch, and directly measures first-action agreement and closed-loop success, so the hit is a provenance threat already covered by the candidate's guard rather than exact-mechanism overlap.
